prompt: Which of the following options gives the correct value of the polynomial p(x) = x<sup>3</sup> - 10x<sup>2</sup> + 3x - 4 at x = -1?
examinerTip: Direct question from PA-2 Class 9 CBSE Mathematics Paper (Question 4).

prompt: Which of the following algebraic expressions is a polynomial?
markingScheme:
• Option (a) has x-1 (negative power) [incorrect]
• Option (c) has x3/2 (fractional power) [incorrect]
• Option (d) has √x = x1/2 [incorrect]
• Option (b) has variable exponents 2, 1, 0 (all whole numbers), so it is a polynomial [1 mark]
examinerTip: Real coefficients can be roots (√3, √2), only variable powers must be whole numbers.

prompt:
Assertion (A): The degree of the polynomial p(x) = 5 is 0.
Reason (R): The degree of a non-zero constant polynomial is always zero, because it can be written as c · x0.
options: (a) Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
(b) Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A).
answer: (a) Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
markingScheme:
• Identifying that constant 5 = 5x0 [0.5 mark]
• Recognizing that degree is the power of variable which is 0 [0.5 mark]
examinerTip: Note: For the zero polynomial p(x) = 0, the degree is NOT defined.

prompt:
Find the zero of each of the following linear polynomials:
(i) p(x) = 3x - 5
(ii) q(x) = ax + b, where a ≠ 0 and a, b are real constants.
answer:
(i) For p(x) = 0: 3x - 5 = 0 ⇒ 3x = 5 ⇒ x = 5/3.
(ii) For q(x) = 0: ax + b = 0 ⇒ ax = -b ⇒ x = -b/a.
markingScheme:
• Correct solution for (i): 1 mark
• Correct solution for (ii): 1 mark
examinerTip: Always state the zero explicitly as x = -b/a.

prompt:
Find the zero of the polynomial:
p(x) = (x - 2)2 - (x + 2)2.
answer:
We simplify p(x) using the algebraic identity a2 - b2 = (a - b)(a + b) [or by direct expansion]:
Method 1 (Expansion):
(x - 2)2 = x2 - 4x + 4
(x + 2)2 = x2 + 4x + 4
p(x) = (x2 - 4x + 4) - (x2 + 4x + 4)
p(x) = x2 - 4x + 4 - x2 - 4x - 4
p(x) = -8x.

To find the zero, set p(x) = 0:
-8x = 0 ⇒ x = 0.
Thus, 0 is the only zero of p(x).
markingScheme:
• Correct expansion of (x - 2)2 and (x + 2)2: 1 mark
• Correct simplification to -8x: 1 mark
• Setting -8x = 0 and obtaining x = 0: 1 mark
examinerTip: From School Exam PA-2 Q31. Make sure to distribute the negative sign carefully.

prompt:
Let p(x) = 2x3 - kx2 + 3x - 6.
(i) If x = 2 is a zero of the polynomial p(x), find the value of the constant k. (2m)
(ii) After substituting the value of k, evaluate p(-2) and p(1/2). (2m)
(iii) Determine the degree and the coefficient of x2 in the resulting polynomial. (1m)
answer:
(i) Since x = 2 is a zero of p(x), p(2) = 0:
p(2) = 2(2)3 - k(2)2 + 3(2) - 6 = 0
2(8) - 4k + 6 - 6 = 0
16 - 4k = 0 ⇒ 4k = 16 ⇒ k = 4.

(ii) The polynomial is p(x) = 2x3 - 4x2 + 3x - 6.
• p(-2) = 2(-2)3 - 4(-2)2 + 3(-2) - 6
= 2(-8) - 4(4) - 6 - 6 = -16 - 16 - 6 - 6 = -44.
• p(1/2) = 2(1/2)3 - 4(1/2)2 + 3(1/2) - 6
= 2(1/8) - 4(1/4) + 3/2 - 6
= 1/4 - 1 + 3/2 - 6 = 1/4 + 6/4 - 4/4 - 24/4 = (1 + 6 - 4 - 24)/4 = -21/4 = -5.25.

(iii) Degree = 3 (highest power of x is 3).
Coefficient of x2 = -4.
markingScheme:
• (i) Setting p(2) = 0 and solving for k = 4: 2 marks
• (ii) Calculating p(-2) = -44 (1 mark) and p(1/2) = -21/4 (1 mark): 2 marks
• (iii) Degree = 3 (0.5 mark) and coefficient of x2 = -4 (0.5 mark): 1 mark
examinerTip: When asked for the coefficient of a term, always include its sign (i.e. -4, not just 4).
